source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Applies when potassium permanganate grains are placed in water and the colour spreads without manual stirring is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Particles of liquids and gases are in constant motion; moving water particles spread potassium permanganate through water, moving gas particles spread fragrance through air, and hotter water spreads the colour faster because its particles move faster. constant particle motion, with faster motion at higher temperature -> spreading and mixing through the available liquid or gas The learner predicts spreading of colour or fragrance from constant particle motion and predicts fastest colour spreading in hot water because hotter particles move faster. Colour or fragrance spreads only when someone stirs, blows, or carries it across the space.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Particulate nature of matter. The student must decide: Decide why colour or fragrance spreads through a liquid or gas, and how temperature changes the rate of spreading in water. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
